page.layout: One printed page of text, full width, with no marginal notes. Top: page number at left and running head at right. Below: verse lines in italic, a dedication heading in capitals, a divider rule, an epitaph heading, and the epitaph verse. At the foot right: the catchword "Aliud".

p.i: Vixit, qui Vitam impendit Vobisque mihique. Ergo, VRSINE, abfit nobisque, tibique, Deoque Vt te Viuentem, demceps [?] ceu lumine cassum Ploremus stulti, quem tot tantique labores, Æternum æterna consecrauere saluti. Et quibus hosce lupos tecum Vi strictibus armis Fregimus, in media, nobis quum morte relinquas, Nempe etiam nobis Vere post funera, Viuis, Et Viues donec cœlorum regia tecum Felici excipiat functos certamine cunctos.

main_text.head: ZACHARIÆ VRSINO SILESIO, VIRO IN OMNI DISCIPLINARVM GENERE EXERCITATISSIMO, THEOLOGO SVMMO, VITÆ INCVLPATÆ, IVDICIO ADMIRABILI, LABORE INDEFESSO, TH. BEZA CHARISSIMO IN CHRISTO FRATRI, P.
EPITAPHIVM D. ZACH. VRSINO SCRIPTVM A LAMBERTO LVDOLPHO PITHOPOEO, Dauentriensi.
main_text.p: Hic Vrsine iaces, Vbi parua Neapolis amplas De Nemetum paruo flumine fundit opes. Inclyta progenuit te Vratislauia, mentem Artibus erudiit Leucoris alma tuam, Lipsia, Parrisij, Tigurum, Basilea, Geneua, Largiter has donis excoluere suis, Estelberga [?] decem, septemque Neapolis annos, Quinque est ingenii dotibus aucta tui: Consilio, dextra, sonuere & voce diserta Sincere Christus, templa scholaque tua. Immodico tandem studij Vitaque labore Ereptus nobis, conderis hoc tumulo. Magnus eras totum, dum Sixti, Vrsine, per orbem, Sed tua post mortem gloria maior erit. Pestis eras viuens: moriens, damnosa Papatus Mors eris antiqui, & certa ruina noui. Cum lacrymis, pietas, doctrina, modestia, candor, Corporis exuuias hic posuere tui.

page.notes: The verse block at the top is a continuation from the previous page, so the first paragraph is marked cont="true". "demceps" is uncertain and marked [?]. "Estelberga" is uncertain and marked [?]. The initial H of the epitaph is a large initial, joined to "ic". Some lines in the top verse may be set with a long-s-like shape in "strictibus"; read as printed. Faint show-through and neighbouring-page text along the right edge are not transcribed.
